extracted.intended_audience: applicants, registered patent practitioners, and USPTO/TC staff who handle receipt and processing of patent correspondence
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and substantive standards for filing patent correspondence (mail, facsimile, or electronic), claiming filing dates via Certificates of Mailing/Transmission or Priority Mail Express®, and related Office handling and petition processes under 35 U.S.C. 21 and 37 CFR 1.8/1.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Technology Center (TC) facilities: access and conduct rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of the TC facilities is strictly limited to the regular business hours of the USPTO (8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on regular business days). Authorized Officials include Supervisory Patent Examiners and TC Directors. No records or other documents of the USPTO shall be removed from the TC facilities except by express written authorization by an authorized official in the TC where the material resides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibitions include use of dictation/reproducing/photographic equipment without prior permission; all packages and personal effects are subject to search and must be removed when leaving; verbal requests from authorized officials must be promptly complied with. Violators may be denied facility use, prosecuted, and may have their names forwarded to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline. Supervisors should courteously request compliance and prepare memoranda detailing incidents to the Deputy Commissioner for Patents via the TC Director. Supervisory Patent Examiners and TC Directors may demand surrender of User or Visitor badges on-the-spot and must follow up with memoranda.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.10 for Priority Mail Express® interruptions (returned mail)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.10(g) — If correspondence sent by Priority Mail Express® is returned by USPS due to an interruption or emergency in service, a person may petition the Director to consider the correspondence filed on a particular date provided certain conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition requirements: (1) petition filed promptly after learning of the return; (2) Priority Mail Express® mailing label number was placed on the papers/fees prior to mailing; (3) petition includes the original correspondence or a copy showing the mailing label number and a copy of the Priority Mail Express® mailing label showing the “date accepted”; and (4) petition includes a statement establishing to the Director's satisfaction the original deposit and that the correspondence/copy is the original or a true copy. The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.10 for Priority Mail Express® refusals (USPS refusal)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.10(h) — If Priority Mail Express® correspondence was refused by a USPS employee due to an interruption/emergency, a person may petition the Director to consider it filed on a particular date if specific conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition requirements: (1) filed promptly after learning of the refusal; (2) mailing label number was placed on the papers prior to attempted mailing; (3) petition includes the original correspondence or a copy showing the mailing label number; and (4) petition includes a statement by the person who attempted to deposit the correspondence establishing the original attempt and that the correspondence/copy is the original or a true copy. The Office may require additional evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions under 37 CFR 1.10 when unable to deposit due to designated interruption/emergency
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.10(i) — When a person was unable to deposit correspondence with the USPS because of a Director-designated interruption/emergency in Priority Mail Express® service, the person may petition the Director to consider the correspondence filed on a particular date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petition requirements: (1) petition filed in the manner designated by the Director promptly after awareness of the designated interruption/emergency; (2) petition includes the original correspondence or a copy; and (3) petition includes a statement establishing, to the Director's satisfaction, that the correspondence would have been deposited but for the designated interruption/emergency and that the correspondence or copy is the original or a true copy. Authority for this practice is 35 U.S.C. 21(a). Note: these provisions apply only to postal interruptions/emergencies, not to other exigencies (e.g., computer failure or inaccessibility of non-USPS facilities). The correspondence must have been complete and ready to be deposited on the requested filing date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority Mail Express® address and service restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: The addresses for Priority Mail Express® to the USPTO are set forth in 37 CFR 1.1 (see MPEP § 501). The Office does not pick up mail; do NOT use the 'Hold for Pickup' service option because mail using that option will not reach the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP § 513 for use of the Priority Mail Express® mailing procedure of 37 CFR 1.10. Priority Mail Express® deposits will be accorded the date of deposit with the USPS as the filing date when done in accordance with 37 CFR 1.10.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation to use USPTO patent electronic filing system (Patent Center) when permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office strongly recommends filing new applications and patent-related correspondence via the USPTO patent electronic filing system (Patent Center) whenever permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal Framework for Patent Electronic Filing on www.uspto.gov/PatentLegalFramework gives information on permitted documents. New applications cannot be transmitted by facsimile and are not entitled to a Certificate of Transmission under 37 CFR 1.8. Some limited exceptions (e.g., CPA for design applications) may be transmitted by facsimile but are not entitled to a certificate benefit unless Office records show complete receipt as required by 37 CFR 1.6(f). New applications may also be hand-delivered; see MPEP § 501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate of Mailing or Transmission: when correspondence is considered timely
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.8(a), correspondence required to be filed within a set period will be considered timely if: (i) mailed or transmitted prior to expiration by (A) addressed and deposited as first class mail with USPS, or (B) transmitted by facsimile in accordance with § 1.6(d), or (C) transmitted via USPTO electronic filing system in accordance with § 1.6(a)(4); and (ii) the correspondence includes a certificate for each piece stating the date of deposit or transmission and signed by a person with reasonable basis to expect the mailing/transmission date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The actual date of receipt is used for all other purposes. If a certificate is used, the person signing should have reasonable basis to expect the correspondence would be mailed or transmitted on or before the date indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions where Certificate of Mailing/Transmission benefits do NOT apply
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.8(a)(2) lists situations where Certificates of Mailing/Transmission give no benefit. For patents and patent applications, these include: (A) filing of a national patent application specification and drawing or other correspondence for obtaining an application filing date (including a CPA under § 1.53(d)); (B) papers in trials before the PTAB governed by § 42.6(b); (C) papers in contested cases before PTAB governed by § 41.106(f); (D) filing of an international application for patent; (E) filing correspondence in an international application before U.S. Receiving/Search/Prelim Examining Authorities; (F) filing a copy of the international application and basic national fee to enter national stage per § 1.495(b); (G) filing a written declaration of abandonment under § 1.138; (H) filing a submission under § 1.217 for publication of a redacted copy; (I) filing a third-party submission under § 1.290; (J) calculation of any period of adjustment under § 1.703(f); (K) filing an international design application. Additionally, disciplinary proceeding filings under part 11 are excluded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these categories are excluded, a Certificate of Mailing or Transmission will not render those filings timely for purposes of obtaining filing dates or meeting deadlines where excluded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when certificate indicates timely mailing/transmission but Office has no evidence of receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: If correspondence considered timely under 37 CFR 1.8(a) is not received after a reasonable time, or application is held abandoned or a proceeding dismissed, the party who forwarded the correspondence must: (1) inform the Office promptly of the previous mailing/transmission; (2) supply an additional copy of the previously mailed/transmitted correspondence and certificate; and (3) include a statement attesting on personal knowledge or to the Director's satisfaction to the previous timely mailing/transmission. Supporting evidence (fax transmission report or electronic acknowledgement receipt) may be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may require additional evidence to determine timeliness. Submissions under these paragraphs in TCs should be forwarded to the Office of Petitions to be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certificate formatting, signature, and attachment requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Certification requires a signature. If the certification appears on a paper that requires a signature, two signatures are required (one for the paper and one for the certification). Though not required, it is preferred the certificate be signed by the applicant or registered practitioner. When possible the certification should appear on the paper being submitted; if insufficient space, it should be on a separate sheet securely attached.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When on a separate sheet, that sheet must be signed and fully identify and be securely attached to the paper (including application number, filing date, and type of paper). An unsigned certification is unacceptable. If detached, evidence that the sheet was received can be supported by a postcard receipt or a copy of the sheet as mailed; for EFS submissions, an electronic acknowledgement receipt and copy of the sheet may support receipt. For multiple papers in one envelope, each paper must have its own certification attached or part thereof; checks do not require certification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested formats for Certificates of Mailing/Transmission
rubrics_metrics.description: The MPEP reproduces suggested formats for Certificate of Mailing, Certificate of Transmission by Facsimile, and Certificate of Transmission via USPTO electronic filing system to be included with correspondence under 37 CFR 1.8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suggested text includes certifying deposit with USPS as first class mail, facsimile transmission statements with fax number and date, and electronic filing system statements with date. The certificate should include typed/printed name and signature of person signing the certificate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of stamped certification is encouraged
rubrics_metrics.description: Some practitioners place the certification language on the first page of a paper with an inked stamp. Such practice is encouraged because the certification is readily visible and forms an integral part of the paper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stamped certification integrates the certificate into the paper and makes it visible during processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office processing: date stamping and handling of envelopes and postmarks
rubrics_metrics.description: OPAP Mail Center will date stamp the actual date of receipt of all papers and will not attempt to retain envelopes or indicate postal cancellation dates (postmarks) on papers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will continue to stamp date of receipt on mail, facsimile, or electronic filings except those filed under 37 CFR 1.10. Receipt date stamped is the date entered in Office records and used to calculate subsequent deadlines. Fax and EFS have special stamping rules (see separate rubric).

rubrics_metrics.name: Office rules to prevent improper award of certificate benefits (hand-delivery/courier misuse)
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits of 37 CFR 1.8 and 37 CFR 1.10 apply only to documents delivered to the Office by the U.S. Postal Service. Documents delivered by hand or commercial couriers (e.g., Federal Express, DHL, UPS) that include Certificates or Priority Mail Express® labels will not be accorded the benefits; OPAP personnel will annotate such correspondences to alert that benefits do not apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a paper contains a Certificate of Mailing or Priority Mail Express® mailing label but was hand-delivered or delivered by courier, write 'HAND DELIVERED' adjacent to the date stamp and notify applicant in the next Office action using form paragraph (e.g., ¶ 5.04 Benefit of Certificate of Mailing Denied). Misuse of a Certificate or improperly claiming benefits more than a one-time inadvertent error should be reported to the Office of Enrollment and Discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office determination and notation when certificate date is within period for reply
rubrics_metrics.description: If a paper that contains a Certificate is received and the date indicated on the Certificate is within the period for reply, the paper should be considered timely filed. The Office should make a notation adjacent to the Office stamp indicating the certificate type and the date (e.g., 'C of Mail 11/10/97').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Certificate date is after the end of the period for reply, the paper is untimely and no notation is needed. If no Certificate appears and the paper is received after the end of the period for reply, the paper is untimely and may result in abandonment or loss of rights. If the filing deadline falls on a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday in D.C., actions deposited/transmitted and certified on the next succeeding business day are considered timely (37 CFR 1.7).

rubrics_metrics.name: Date-stamping rules for facsimile and USPTO electronic filing system transmissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Per 37 CFR 1.6(a)(3), facsimile transmissions are stamped with the date the complete transmission is received in the Office unless that date is a Saturday, Sunday, or Federal holiday in D.C.; in that case the stamp is the next succeeding non-holiday business day. Per 37 CFR 1.6(a)(4), correspondence submitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system is accorded a receipt date equal to the Eastern Time date/time when received, regardless of weekend or Federal holiday in D.C.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rules affect how receipt dates are recorded and how deadlines are computed; EFS receipts may show receipt on weekends/holidays whereas fax receipts roll to next business day for stamping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Original mailed paper not delivered: forwarding to Office of Petitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraphs (b) and (c) of 37 CFR 1.8 cover situations where a paper containing a Certificate was timely deposited or transmitted but never received by the Office. In the Technology Centers, submissions under these paragraphs should be forwarded to the Office of Petitions for consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow procedures for informing the Office, supplying copies and certificates, and including attestation statements (see the procedure rubric). The Office may require additional evidence to determine timeliness.
